title: Tether Link Utility: Share Your Phone's Mobile Data via SOCKS5
ogTitle: Tether Link Utility: Share Your Phone's Mobile Data via SOCKS5
description: Share your Android phone's mobile data with your laptop, tablet or another phone through a local SOCKS5 proxy. No root, no account, no remote server.

howTo.name: How to share your phone's mobile data over Wi-Fi with Tether Link Utility

steps.name: Tap START
steps.text: The Wi-Fi hotspot turns on automatically. The app creates a local SOCKS5 proxy tunnel and displays the connection details.

steps.name: Show the QR code
steps.text: One QR code carries the Wi-Fi network and the proxy address together. The network name and password are also shown as plain text for laptops.

steps.name: Connect your device
steps.text: Android: scan the QR code to join the Wi-Fi and connect the proxy automatically. Windows / macOS / iOS: install your proxy app first (the phone's Wi-Fi may show "No internet"; that's normal), then join the Wi-Fi shown and enter the IP and port in your SOCKS5 proxy settings.

steps.name: Start browsing
steps.text: Traffic routes through your mobile data. No remote server, everything stays on your device.

how.title: Connected in four steps

before.title: Before you start
before.lead: You need at least two devices: one phone shares its mobile data, your other devices connect to it.

roles.title: This phone
lines: Turn on mobile data. Open the app in Share mode, tap START SHARING, then Show QR code.

roles.title: Your other devices
lines: Android phone with the app: tap Share mode at the top, choose Use another phone's internet and follow the steps.
Windows, Mac or Linux: on the sharing phone, open Connection help, pick the device type and apply the recommended settings.

before.help: Stuck? Open Connection help in the app.

steps.text: The hotspot turns on automatically and the proxy starts.

steps.title: Show QR code
steps.text: One code carries the Wi-Fi network and the proxy address.

steps.title: Connect your device

cards.title: Fully local
cards.text: The proxy runs on your phone. No account and no remote server: your routed traffic is never sent to our servers or logged by the proxy. The free version shows ads, and our ad provider may collect device identifiers. See the Privacy Policy.

cards.title: Android-to-Android auto connect
cards.text: Scan the QR code on the other Android phone; on most devices Wi-Fi joins and the proxy connects automatically.

cards.title: IP change alerts
cards.text: Carrier IPs can change between sessions. The app notices the change and alerts connected devices automatically.

how.notes: Using your phone's own hotspot? If you turn on Mobile Hotspot (Android) or Personal Hotspot (iPhone) yourself, save its name and password once with Add hotspot Wi-Fi details in the app. They stay on your device, the hotspot itself isn't changed, and they're added to the QR code so other devices join by scanning. Not needed when the Android app starts its own hotspot. Data used by connected devices counts toward your mobile plan. Check your carrier's terms for tethering.

items.q: How does Tether Link Utility work?
items.a: It runs a local SOCKS5 proxy on your Android phone, using Android's VpnService API, and shares it over the phone's Wi-Fi hotspot (no USB cable involved). Your other devices send their traffic to that proxy, and the phone forwards it over its mobile data connection. There's no remote server in between.
No, it works entirely without root privileges.

items.q: Does it use a remote server?
items.a: No. Proxied traffic goes from your devices to your phone and out over your mobile data; it is not routed through, logged, or stored on any server of ours. The free version shows Google AdMob ads, and the app uses Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, which collect device identifiers and usage and crash data, as described in our privacy policy.

items.q: Can I connect a Windows or Mac laptop?
items.a: Yes, point your laptop's SOCKS5 proxy settings (built into macOS, or via Firefox/FoxyProxy on Windows) at the IP and port shown in the app. That covers apps which check that setting; for full system-wide coverage including DNS, use sing-box in TUN mode instead.

items.q: Does a SOCKS5 proxy setting protect all my traffic?
items.a: Not entirely. A browser or system SOCKS5 setting only reroutes traffic from apps that check it; DNS lookups and other background traffic can still go over the plain hotspot connection instead of the proxy. For full coverage on Windows or macOS, run sing-box in TUN mode, which routes your whole system's traffic, DNS included, through the tunnel.

iOS has no native SOCKS5 setting, but apps like Shadowrocket or Potatso can connect to the proxy the same way, for that app's own traffic only, not the whole device. A verified full-device option isn't currently available on iOS. A native iOS app is in development and coming soon.

items.q: How many devices can connect at once?
items.a: The free tier connects 1 device at a time; Pro raises that to 5. Pro starts from $3.99/month. The exact price, including local currency and yearly plan, is shown in Google Play or the App Store.
Yes, it shares whatever active mobile data connection your phone currently has, regardless of network generation.

items.q: Does it use my mobile data plan?
items.a: Yes. Data used by connected devices counts toward your plan. Check your carrier's terms for tethering.

Yes, the free version is free to use: 1 device at a time, with ads. Pro removes ads and allows up to 5 devices at once. The app itself doesn't currently add a speed limit; actual speed depends on your carrier, plan and signal.

items.q: Can other devices join my own hotspot by scanning the QR code?
items.a: Yes. If you turn on your phone's system hotspot yourself (Mobile Hotspot on Android, Personal Hotspot on iPhone), save its network name and password once with Add hotspot Wi-Fi details in the app. They are stored only on your device, the app doesn't change your hotspot settings, and the details are added to the QR code so other devices join the network automatically by scanning. On iPhone, the password is shown in Settings > Personal Hotspot. When the Android app starts its own hotspot automatically, this step isn't needed.
